battle.name: 波蘭王位繼承戰爭
battle.theater: 馬佐維亞與維斯瓦河下游
battle.brief: 一七三三年二月奧古斯特二世病逝，王位懸空；八月俄軍入波、十月初戰事全面爆發，萊什琴斯基退守但澤，一七三四年二月至六月遭俄薩聯軍圍城而陷。聯邦省級步兵仍以長槍兵與火槍兵混編作戰，長槍守住砲隊、營壘與缺口，直到一七三六年的調解議會把聯邦處境定案。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 一七三三年的波蘭王位繼承戰爭，是在外邦干涉下重演的一場王位繼承危機，而且主戰場大部分不在波蘭境內。支持前王斯坦尼斯勞夫·萊什琴斯基的一邊是波旁王朝聯盟：法國、西班牙、薩伏依與帕爾馬公國；反對的一邊是俄羅斯、薩克森選侯奧古斯特三世、奧地利哈布斯堡王朝，帝國自一七三四年起也正式參戰，加上普魯士。聯邦自身則被劈成兩塊：一七三三年九月十日的選舉議會以貴族與民眾的廣泛支持選出萊什琴斯基，同年十月的第二次選舉議會則推舉奧古斯特三世，兩派各自成立省邦聯盟並組織民兵。聯邦的軍事結構是波蘭王國軍與立陶宛軍兩支常備職業軍，加上各省民兵與長槍農兵，總數雖可湊到十萬以上，卻分散在各省、常備不足、裝備參差。俄羅斯由女皇安娜與掌樞密院的大臣奧斯特爾曼主持政策，戰場上以彼得·拉齊、穆尼希等將領率領俄軍步兵與哥薩克，並以薩克森部隊充當先鋒與攻城骨幹。奧地利在萊什琴斯基之女瑪麗亞·約瑟法已與洛林的弗朗茨·斯特凡訂婚的名義下支持他，卻把主力留在萊茵河與義大利，結果在南北西三面幾乎沒有可依靠的外部盟友。法國要的是削弱哈布斯堡、把波蘭當籌碼，於是把主力投向萊茵河與義大利，法薩聯軍攻入米蘭、拿勒斯與西西里，卻沒能把萊什琴斯基扶上王座。英國與荷蘭保持中立，荷蘭還因懼怕戰事重來而擴軍；普魯士則在聯邦內戰中趁火打劫，兼併西普魯士。
countriesEn: The War of the Polish Succession of 1733 was a succession crisis re-enacted under foreign intervention, and most of the fighting took place outside Poland itself. The side supporting the former king Stanisław Leszczyński was the Bourbon alliance: France, Spain, Savoy and the Duchy of Parma. The side against him was Russia, the Saxon elector Augustus III, the Austrian Habsburg monarchy, the Holy Roman Empire from 1734, and Prussia. The Commonwealth itself was split in two: an election sejm on 10 September 1733 elected Leszczyński with broad support from the nobility and the populace, and a second election sejm in October of the same year proclaimed Augustus III; each side formed provincial confederations and raised its own militia. The military structure of the Commonwealth was two professional standing armies, the Army of the Crown and the Army of Lithuania, together with the militia of the provinces and the peasant pikemen; the total could be raised to something over a hundred thousand, but it was scattered, thin in permanent troops and uneven in equipment. Russia was directed by Empress Anna and by Osterman, with commanders such as Peter Lacy and Münnich leading the Russian infantry and Cossacks, Saxon troops forming the spearhead and the battering ram of the assaults. Austria supported Leszczyński on the ground that his daughter Maria Josepha was already betrothed to Francis Stephen of Lorraine, but kept its main strength in the Rhineland and in Italy, and found itself on its southern and western frontiers with hardly any effective external allies. France wanted to weaken the Habsburgs and to use Poland as a bargaining counter, so it put its strength into the Rhineland and Italy: French and Sardinian troops entered Milan, Naples and Sicily, yet could not put Leszczyński on the throne. Britain and the Dutch Republic stayed neutral, the Dutch even enlarging their army for fear of another war, while Prussia seized the opportunity of the civil war in the Commonwealth to annex Royal Prussia.
people: 這場戰爭裡的關鍵人物分屬四個方向。波蘭一邊的核心是奧古斯特二世與他的兒子奧古斯特三世：老王一七三三年二月一日病逝於華沙，年僅四十歲；新王一七三三年十月的第二次選舉議會上只靠少數人當選，一七三四年一月十七日在克拉科夫的瓦維爾大教堂加冕，一七六三年十月五日卒於德累斯頓。萊什琴斯基一方最不可替代的是萊什琴斯基本人與他的妻子瑪麗（瑪麗·萊什琴斯卡，一七二五年嫁路易十五，法國因此以岳母身分成為他的靠山），此外還有波蘭大主教西奧多·安德熱伊·波托茨基、法國與瑞典派駐的公使，以及在但澤解圍之役中率八千人出動的亞當·塔爾沃；加里西亞的尼古拉·波托茨基伯爵也曾企圖以兵力支援他。俄羅斯的關鍵人物是女皇安娜、奧斯特爾曼、野戰統帥彼得·拉齊與穆尼希，另有海軍提督托馬斯·戈登率艦隊入波。奧地利方面是歐根親王、塞肯多夫、陶恩、梅西與克尼希塞格等將領，奧根在菲利普斯堡解圍時隨行的還有普魯士王儲腓特烈。法國方面，貝里克公爵在菲利普斯堡被砲彈擊斃，維爾吉、布羅意與貝勒伊爾分別統兵，拉佩魯茲、巴拉伊與普萊洛在但澤與海上作戰，普萊洛陣亡。普魯士的腓特烈·威廉一世被皇帝所猜忌，只能有限度地出兵；巴伐利亞的查理·阿爾伯特在一七三三年十一月與法國簽下秘密協議，是日後另一場戰爭的伏線。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities of this war came from four directions. At the centre of the Polish side stood Augustus II and his son Augustus III. The old king died in Warsaw on 1 February 1733 at the age of only forty. The new king was elected by a small minority at the second election sejm in October 1733, was crowned on 17 January 1734 in the Wawel Cathedral at Kraków, and died at Dresden on 5 October 1763. On the Leszczyński side the indispensable figures were Leszczyński himself and his wife Marie Leszczyńska, who married Louis XV in 1725 and made France his patron by way of that marriage; to them may be added Teodor Andrzej Potocki, Primate of Poland, the French and Swedish ministers accredited to the court, Adam Tarło, who led eight thousand men in the attempt to relieve Danzig, and Count Nicholas Potocki in Galicia, who hoped to support Leszczyński with troops. The key Russians were Empress Anna, Osterman, the field commanders Peter Lacy and Münnich, and Admiral Thomas Gordon, who brought a squadron into the Baltic. On the Austrian side were Prince Eugene, Seckendorff, Daun, Mercy and Königsegg; when Eugene attempted to relieve Philippsburg he was accompanied by the Prussian crown prince Frederick. On the French side the Duke of Berwick was killed by a shell at Philippsburg, Villars, Broglie and Belle-Isle commanded in turn, and Lapeyrouse, Barailh and Plélo fought at Danzig and at sea, Plélo being killed. Frederick William I of Prussia was distrusted by the emperor and could only give limited assistance, and Charles-Albert of Bavaria signed a secret agreement with France in November 1733, which was to be the fuse of a later war.
kits: 長槍在這場戰爭裡的位置，是歐洲火槍化的最後一截尾巴。俄軍、薩克森軍與普軍在一七三〇年代初都已把長槍換成火槍配刺刀，彼得大帝早在一七〇〇年前後於俄國步軍中取消長槍，普魯士軍隊更早在一七〇三年就廢棄長槍改用插座刺刀，奧地利與薩克森亦在十八世紀初陸續改裝。因此本場戰爭裡真正還靠長槍作戰的是波蘭立陶宛聯邦的部隊：聯邦的省級步兵仍按傳統分成長槍兵與火槍兵兩種營，貴族自備的城鄉民兵與所謂長槍農兵手持三至四公尺的直木長槍，主要任務是守住營壘、護住砲車、封鎖缺口、對抗騎兵衝鋒，在但澤的城牆、內城與街巷裡仍是比火槍更可靠的近戰手段；火槍兵負責射擊，兩者在方陣中交替排列，長槍在前、火槍在其後。但澤圍城之役的守方清單恰好說明這一點：城內除四個王國軍團外，還有七千五百至八千五百名波蘭民兵與義勇、一千二百七十九名近衛民兵、兩千一百五十名近衛騎兵，以及約二千四百名法軍（另有說法指一千二百至一千八百人，其中一千二百名為龍騎兵）與一百三十至二百名瑞典義勇，這些民兵與義勇手中的長槍就是城頭與街壘的最後支撐。砲兵方面，聯軍初時火力不足，俄軍的推進一度被自家火炮數量拖住，直到一七三四年五月重型攻城砲與一萬名薩克森兵到位，才攻下維斯瓦河口的外堡，再在強攻海格堡時被擊退。攻城靠壕溝、砲壘與封鎖維斯瓦河口，法國的接應船隊與海上砲火亦參與其事。
kitsEn: The pike occupies in this war the last stub of Europe's pike-and-shot age. The Russian, Saxon and Prussian armies had all exchanged the pike for the musket and bayonet in the early 1730s: Peter the Great had abolished the pike in Russian infantry around 1700, the Prussian army had dropped it even earlier, in 1703, for the socket bayonet, and Austria and Saxony followed through the first decades of the century. The troops that really fought with pikes in this war therefore belonged to the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, whose provincial infantry still followed the old division into pikemen and musketeers; the town and country militias raised by the nobles and the so-called peasant pikemen carried straight wooden pikes three to four metres long, their tasks being to hold the camp, to guard the guns, to close breaches, to withstand cavalry charges, and inside the walls, the inner city and the streets of Danzig they remained a more reliable close-combat arm than the musket; the musketeers shot, the two stood in the same formation with pikes in front and muskets behind. The order of battle of the defenders at Danzig illustrates the point exactly: besides four regiments of the Crown army the city held some seven thousand five hundred to eight thousand five hundred Polish militiamen and volunteers, one thousand two hundred and seventy-nine men of the Guards militia and two thousand one hundred and fifty Guards cavalrymen, together with about two thousand four hundred French (other counts give one thousand two hundred to one thousand eight hundred, of whom one thousand two hundred were dragoons) and one hundred thirty to two hundred Swedish volunteers; the pikes in the hands of these militiamen and volunteers were the last prop of the ramparts and the barricades. On the artillery side the besiegers were at first short of guns, and the Russian advance was held up by the shortage of their own ordnance until heavy siege pieces and ten thousand Saxons arrived in May 1734; only then was the outwork at the mouth of the Vistula taken, and the attempt to storm the Hagelburg was bloodily beaten back. The siege rested on trenches, batteries and the sealing of the Vistula mouth, and the French relief squadron with its naval gunfire took part.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術樣貌與同時代的線狀戰爭明顯不同：波蘭與立陶宛的領土太大、城池太多，決定勝負的往往不是野戰而是圍城與行軍，而整場戰爭的大半又在聯邦境外進行。聯軍在波蘭方面的方針是「不求速決、以城市為支點」：一七三三年八月俄軍入波逼選，九月底彼得·拉齊率兩萬人進入華沙，萊什琴斯基帶著華沙僅有的兩千人退守但澤，聯軍隨即在但澤周圍展開長達四個月的圍城。圍城的技術過程清楚可考：一七三四年二月二日至六月三十日，聯軍先以水壩與砲壘封住波蘭灣，再自維斯瓦河口的外堡逐段向城內迫近；三月十七日穆尼希率一萬五千援軍抵達、接掌指揮，圍城軍總數增至六萬人；五月重型攻城砲與一萬名薩克森兵到位後，外堡被攻下，強攻海格堡卻被守軍擊退；亞當·塔爾沃率八千人往解圍，在貝倫特一帶遭拉齊的支隊突襲而敗退；法國的接應船隊再到，戰局仍在城牆之下僵持；最後守軍於六月底投降，萊什琴斯基喬裝成農夫在城陷前兩日逃出，經柯尼斯堡發出宣言、重組省邦聯盟，並派使赴巴黎要求法國以至少四萬人入侵薩克森。境外方面，法國與薩伏依聯軍於一七三三年十月十日以五萬餘人進入米蘭，而奧軍守軍僅約一萬二千人，米蘭在十一月三日即告易手，隨後拿勒斯陷落，西西里各要塞迅速屈服；一七三四年五月二十五日比通托一役法薩聯軍擊敗奧軍，四月開始的加埃塔圍城於八月陷落，卡普阿守到十一月。萊茵河方面，貝里克公爵圍攻菲利普斯堡兩個月，該堡於一七三四年七月陷落，貝里克本人被砲彈擊斃；法軍推進至美因茨，歐根親王終於在一七三五年十月克勞森之戰被辛肯多夫率三萬人擊退。其整體邏輯是：以城市、河流與補給線取勝，而非以會戰取勝；每一次圍城都是對糧秣與彈藥的消耗戰，而俄軍一度因攻城砲不足而無法推進，正是這種消耗結構的寫照。
tacticsEn: The character of the warfare differed sharply from the linear warfare of the same decade, because Poland and Lithuania had too much territory and too many towns, so that what usually decided the outcome was the siege and the march rather than the field battle, and because most of the war was fought outside the Commonwealth altogether. The allied plan in Poland was to take no risks on speed and to make the towns their anchors: Russian troops entered Poland in August 1733 to influence the election, Peter Lacy entered Warsaw with twenty thousand men at the end of September, and Leszczyński, with the two thousand men he had in Warsaw, withdrew to Danzig, where the allies opened a siege that lasted four months. The technical course of that siege is well documented: from 22 February to 30 June 1734 the besiegers first dammed the Polish Bay and worked their batteries round the city, then pressed inward from the outwork at the mouth of the Vistula; on 17 March Münnich arrived with fifteen thousand reinforcements and took over the command, bringing the besieging army to sixty thousand men; in May, with heavy siege guns and ten thousand Saxons in hand, the outwork was taken but the storm of the Hagelburg was beaten back; Adam Tarło led eight thousand men to relieve the city and was surprised by a detachment of Lacy near Berent and repulsed; a French relief squadron arrived and the deadlock at the walls continued; the garrison capitulated at the end of June, and two days before the city fell Leszczyński escaped disguised as a peasant, made his way to Königsberg, issued a manifesto that reconstituted a confederation on his behalf and sent an envoy to Paris urging France to invade Saxony with at least forty thousand men. Outside Poland, French and Sardinian troops numbering over fifty thousand entered Milanese territory on 10 October 1733 against some twelve thousand Austrians, and Milan itself fell on 3 November, followed by the capture of Naples and the rapid submission of the Sicilian fortresses; the French and Sardinian army defeated the Austrians at Bitonto on 25 May 1734, Gaeta, invested from April, surrendered in August, and Capua held out until November. In the Rhineland the Duke of Berwick invested Philippsburg for two months and the fortress fell in July 1734, Berwick himself being killed by a shell; the French pushed to Mainz, and Prince Eugene was finally driven back by Seckendorff with thirty thousand men at Clausen in October 1735. The underlying logic was to win by towns, rivers and lines of supply rather than by pitched battles: every investment was a war of attrition upon food and ammunition, and the Russian advance was at one point held up by a shortage of siege artillery, which is exactly what such an attrition structure produces.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。戰爭自一七三三年八月至十月在波蘭境內爆發，至一七三五年十月達成初步停戰，一七三八年十一月《維也納條約》正式終結，前後約五年。兵員與日期：八一十一日拉齊率三萬俄軍入波；九月底拉齊的兩萬人進入華沙；十月六日的第二次選舉議會推舉奧古斯特三世；一七三四年二月二日至六月三十日但澤圍城，聯軍初兵一萬二千、總數三萬七千至六萬，守軍初兵四千五百、總數約二萬四千四百四十五人，包括王國軍五個團至少七千人、波蘭民兵與義勇七千五百至八千五百人、近衛民兵一千二百七十九人、近衛騎兵兩千一百五十人、法軍約二千四百人（另有說法為一千二百至一千八百人，其中一千二百名龍騎兵）與瑞典義勇一百三十至二百人；三月十七日穆尼希率一萬五千人到達；五月重型攻城砲與一萬名薩克森兵抵達，聯軍攻下維斯瓦河口外堡；亞當·塔爾沃率八千人解圍失利。傷亡方面，據俄軍史家涅利波維奇的統計，攻城軍陣亡八百零一人、受傷一千七百五十三人、失蹤十二人（另一說合計約八千人），守軍損失未見確數；全歐洲戰線的軍人亡故，據二〇一四年出版的《War in the Modern Great Power System》統計約八萬八千人。境外戰線：法薩聯軍五萬餘人對奧軍約一萬二千人；萊茵河方面辛肯多夫率三萬人作戰。領土變動最能說明戰局：波蘭放棄對庫爾蘭公國的直接控制權與對立窩尼亞的主張，奧地利取得帕爾馬公國與加里西亞，萊什琴斯基獲洛林與巴爾，弗朗茨·斯特凡獲托斯卡納。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war broke out in Poland between August and October 1733, a preliminary peace was reached in October 1735, and the Treaty of Vienna closed it formally in November 1738, a matter of about five years. On men and dates: on 11 August Lacy entered Poland with thirty thousand Russian troops; at the end of September Lacy's twenty thousand entered Warsaw; on 6 October the second election sejm proclaimed Augustus III; the siege of Danzig ran from 22 February to 30 June 1734, the besiegers numbering twelve thousand at the outset and thirty-seven to sixty thousand in total, the defenders four thousand five hundred at the outset and some twenty-four thousand four hundred and forty-five in all, made up of at least seven thousand men in five regiments of the Crown army, seven thousand five hundred to eight thousand five hundred Polish militiamen and volunteers, one thousand two hundred and seventy-nine men of the Guards militia, two thousand one hundred and fifty Guards cavalrymen, about two thousand four hundred French (other counts give one thousand two hundred to one thousand eight hundred, of whom one thousand two hundred were dragoons) and one hundred thirty to two hundred Swedish volunteers; on 17 March Münnich arrived with fifteen thousand men; in May the heavy guns and ten thousand Saxons arrived and the outwork at the mouth of the Vistula fell; Adam Tarło's eight thousand men were beaten back in the attempt to relieve the city. On losses, the Russian military historian Nelipovich gives for the besieging army eight hundred and one killed, one thousand seven hundred and fifty-three wounded and twelve missing, with another count putting the total at about eight thousand, while no firm figure is recorded for the defenders; for the war as a whole, the military deaths across all European fronts are put at about eighty-eight thousand in War in the Modern Great Power System, published in 2014. On the theatres outside Poland: more than fifty thousand French and Sardinian troops against some twelve thousand Austrians in Italy, and thirty thousand men under Seckendorff on the Rhine. The territorial changes show the state of the war most clearly: Poland gave up direct control of the Duchy of Courland and its claims to Livonia, Austria received the Duchy of Parma and Galicia, Leszczyński was awarded Lorraine and Bar, and Francis Stephen received the Grand Duchy of Tuscany.
cause: 打起來有四層原因。最內層是聯邦本身的憲政結構：波蘭立陶宛聯邦是選舉王國，王位由選舉議會推舉，新王必須簽署王位條件，而一七三二年聯邦議會決議驅逐境內的俄國與薩克森駐軍，此舉同時得罪了兩個王朝。國際層面更早埋下伏筆：秘密的《三黑鷹條約》（一七三二年）由俄羅斯、奧地利與普魯士訂立，三國同意反對萊什琴斯基與奧古斯特三世當選，改推葡萄牙的曼努埃爾王子；換言之，兩個主要候選人其實都被三大國排除了。當老王一七三三年二月一日病逝，選舉立刻被外部力量接管：奧古斯特三世在同年七月分別與俄國和奧地利達成密約，向俄國交出波蘭對立窩尼亞的剩餘主張、承諾讓安娜女皇自行指定庫爾蘭公國的繼承人，向皇帝承諾承認一七一三年的《波拉日克詔令》；八月十一日拉齊率三萬俄軍入波施壓，萊什琴斯基被迫帶著華沙僅有的兩千人退入但澤；九月十日的選舉議會以貴族與民眾的廣泛支持、以及法國與瑞典的背書選出萊什琴斯基，九月底俄軍占領華沙，十月六日的第二次選舉議會則推舉奧古斯特三世。第四層是列強的自身算盤：法國的目標是拆散哈布斯堡的聯盟網，趁俄奧被波蘭戰事拖住時在義大利奪取洛林、米蘭、拿勒斯與西西里，並利用萊什琴斯基的女兒瑪麗·萊什琴斯卡是路易十五王后這層關係；西班牙與薩伏依各圖自己的義大利領地；帝國自一七三四年起正式出兵以守意大利，但南北西三面都缺盟友；普魯士則趁聯邦內亂兼併西普魯士。英國與荷蘭保持中立，英國以一七三一年《維也納條約》只是防禦性條約、且奧地利是進攻方為由，把不參戰寫成政策。
causeEn: There were four layers of cause. The innermost was the constitutional structure of the Commonwealth: it was an elective monarchy, the crown chosen by an election sejm, and a new king had to swear the conditions of kingship, while the Sejm's resolution of 1732 to expel the Russian and Saxon garrisons from Polish territory offended two dynasties at once. The international layer was laid down even earlier: in the secret Treaty of the Three Black Eagles of 1732, Russia, Austria and Prussia agreed to oppose the election of either Leszczyński or Augustus III and to back the Portuguese Infante Manuel instead; in other words, both principal candidates had been ruled out beforehand by the three great powers. When the old king died on 1 February 1733 the election was immediately taken over from outside: in July 1733 Augustus III concluded separate agreements with Russia and Austria, giving Russia Poland's remaining claims to Livonia and promising Empress Anna her own choice of successor to the Duchy of Courland, and promising the emperor recognition of the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713; on 11 August Lacy entered Poland with thirty thousand Russian troops, and Leszczyński was forced to withdraw with the two thousand men he had in Warsaw into Danzig; the election sejm of 10 September elected him with broad support from the nobility and the populace and with the backing of France and Sweden, the Russians occupied Warsaw at the end of September, and the second election sejm of 6 October proclaimed Augustus III. The fourth layer was the calculation of the powers themselves. France's purpose was to break up the Habsburg network of alliances and, while Russia and Austria were absorbed in Poland, to take Lorraine, Milan, Naples and Sicily in Italy, using the fact that Leszczyński's daughter Marie Leszczyńska was queen of France; Spain and Savoy each had their own Italian claims in view; the Empire entered the war formally from 1734 to hold Italy, but had no allies on its southern or western frontiers; and Prussia used the civil war in the Commonwealth to annex Royal Prussia. Britain and the Dutch Republic stayed neutral, the British justifying non-intervention by the argument that the Treaty of Vienna of 1731 was purely defensive and that Austria was the aggressor.
impact: 影響可以分幾層看。第一層是波蘭立陶宛聯邦本身：這場戰爭暴露並加速了聯邦的崩解。選舉由外國軍隊與外國錢糧決定，萊什琴斯基在位也不過是候選人，聯邦議會在一七三六年的調解議會上實質確認奧古斯特三世為王，同時波蘭交出對庫爾蘭公國的直接控制權與對立窩尼亞的主張，國家獨立的樞紐被從根上抽走；此後奧古斯特三世之外只剩一位波蘭王，即俄國扶持的斯坦尼斯勞夫·奧古斯特，聯邦最終在一七七二年被瓜分，戰爭已經預演了它的結局。第二層是歐洲權力平衡與洛林問題：一七三五年的初步和約與一七三八年的《維也納條約》把洛林與巴爾由帝國領地變成法國的保護地，萊什琴斯基保有至死，死後經其女歸法國；弗朗茨·斯特凡以托斯卡納作補償，最後一位美第奇大公吉安·加斯托尼在一七三七年去世才使這批領土交換落實；奧地利得帕爾馬，帕爾馬的查理取得那不勒斯與西西里兩頂王冠。法國與其盟友在和約中承認《波拉日克詔令》，卻被條目評為空頭保證——一七四〇年查理六世一死，法國仍然插手瓜分哈布斯堡君主國，爆發奧地利王位繼承戰爭；巴伐利亞的查理·阿爾伯特在一七三三年十一月已與法國簽下秘密協議，同樣是那場戰爭的伏線。波蘭王位戰爭因此不是孤立的插曲，而是七年後那場歐洲大戰的引信。第三層是軍備：這是歐洲大陸上最後幾場仍看得到長槍實戰的戰爭之一，波蘭與立陶宛的省級步兵仍以長槍兵與火槍兵混編作戰，俄軍、普軍、薩克森軍與奧軍早已改用火槍配刺刀，戰後長槍全面退出歐洲步兵，只在儀仗與老兵記憶中留下位置。第四層是東南歐：波蘭需要奧地利與土耳其制衡俄國，奧土同盟因此成立，一七三五年至一七三九年的波蘭-土耳其戰爭與俄土戰爭相連，導致一七三九年貝爾格萊德條約，也把俄國的南進壓力推向克里米亞與黑海，之後才有一七六八年至一七七四年的俄土戰爭。第五層是普魯士與但澤：普魯士在西普魯士取得的港口與通行權，使它在一七七二年瓜分中獲得埃爾姆蘭，一七九三年第二次瓜分時得到但澤、托倫與皇家普魯士，成為波蘭西界爭議的源頭。
impactEn: The effects can be read on several levels. The first is the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, for this war exposed and hurried its dissolution. The election was decided by foreign armies and foreign money; Leszczyński's kingship remained that of a candidate; the Sejm of 1736 de facto confirmed Augustus III as king while Poland surrendered direct control of the Duchy of Courland and its claims to Livonia, and the hinge of national independence was pulled out at the root. Only one further king of Poland was to follow Augustus III, Stanisław August, raised by Russia, before the Commonwealth was partitioned in 1772; the war had rehearsed its ending. The second level is the European balance of power and the question of Lorraine. The preliminary peace of 1735 and the Treaty of Vienna of 1738 turned Lorraine and Bar from imperial fiefs into territories under French protection, to be held by Leszczyński for life and to pass to France through his daughter after his death; Francis Stephen received the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in compensation, and the exchange of territories could only be carried out after the death of the last Medici, Gian Gastone, in 1737; Austria received Parma, and Charles of Parma took the crowns of Naples and Sicily. France and its allies recognised the Pragmatic Sanction in the settlement, but this was described as a hollow guarantee: when Charles VI died in 1740 France after all intervened to partition the Habsburg monarchy, and the War of the Austrian Succession broke out; the secret agreement Charles-Albert of Bavaria had signed with France in November 1733 was a fuse for the same war. The Polish war of the succession was therefore not an isolated episode but the primer of the great European war seven years later. The third level is armament: this was one of the last wars on the European continent in which the pike was still fought with in earnest, the provincial infantry of Poland and Lithuania still marching in mixed formations of pikemen and musketeers, while the Russian, Prussian, Saxon and Austrian armies had long gone over to musket and bayonet; after it the pike left European infantry altogether and survived only in ceremony and in the memory of old soldiers. The fourth level is south-eastern Europe: Poland needed Austria and Turkey to hold Russia in check, and the Austro-Turkish alliance was the result; the Polish-Turkish war of 1735 to 1739 ran alongside the Russo-Turkish war and led to the Treaty of Belgrade of 1739, turning Russia's pressure south towards the Crimea and the Black Sea, and so towards the Russo-Turkish wars of 1768 to 1774. The fifth level is Prussia and Danzig: the harbours and the right of passage Prussia acquired in Royal Prussia gave it Ermland in the partition of 1772 and Danzig, Elbląg and Royal Prussia in the partition of 1793, claims that remained at the root of every later dispute over Poland's western frontier.
result: 一七三三年至一七三八年的收場是一連串讓步。一七三三年九月十日選出的萊什琴斯基在但澤堅守到一七三四年六月三十日城陷前一天才喬裝逃出，經柯尼斯堡發出宣言、重組省邦聯盟，並赴巴黎要求法國以至少四萬人入侵薩克森；波蘭境內的主要戰事到此為止。一七三五年十月達成初步停戰，一七三八年十一月《維也納條約》予以批准：奧古斯特三世正式被確認為波蘭王，萊什琴斯基獲洛林與巴爾作補償（他死後經女兒歸法國），弗朗茨·斯特凡以托斯卡納作失去洛林的補償，奧地利取得帕爾馬，帕爾馬的查理取得那不勒斯與西西里，波蘭則交出對庫爾蘭的直接控制權與立窩尼亞主張。但澤在圍城後受損並向勝利者支付賠償，聯邦議會在一七三六年的調解議會上實質確認奧古斯特三世；奧古斯特三世統治至一七六三年十月五日在德累斯頓去世，葬在德累斯頓，此後波蘭只餘一位國王斯坦尼斯勞夫·奧古斯特，聯邦最終在十八世紀末被瓜分。至於長槍：這場戰爭是它在歐洲大陸上最後的實戰歲月，波蘭聯邦的長槍兵在但澤的城頭、街壘與缺口上仍撐住整條防線，但俄軍、薩克森兵與法國援軍的圍城最終靠的是攻城砲與封鎖河口，而不是長槍；幾年之後，連最後保留長槍的歐洲軍隊也換上了刺刀，長槍從此只存在於儀仗、操典與老兵的回憶裡。
resultEn: The outcome of 1733 to 1738 was a series of concessions. Leszczyński, elected on 10 September 1733, held Danzig until the city fell on 30 June 1734 and he escaped disguised as a peasant the day before, made his way to Königsberg, issued a manifesto reconstituting a confederation and went to Paris to ask France to invade Saxony with at least forty thousand men; the main fighting inside Poland ended there. A preliminary peace was concluded in October 1735 and ratified by the Treaty of Vienna in November 1738: Augustus III was formally confirmed as king of Poland, Leszczyński was compensated with the Duchies of Lorraine and Bar, which passed to France through his daughter after his death, Francis Stephen received the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in compensation for losing Lorraine, Austria received the Duchy of Parma, Charles of Parma took the crowns of Naples and Sicily, and Poland surrendered its direct control of Courland together with its claims to Livonia. Danzig was damaged by the siege and paid reparations to the victors, and the Sejm of 1736 de facto confirmed Augustus III, who reigned until his death at Dresden on 5 October 1763, where he was buried; only one king of Poland was left after him, Stanisław August, and the Commonwealth was finally partitioned at the end of the eighteenth century. As for the pike: this war was its last season of real fighting on the European continent. The pikemen of the Polish Commonwealth still held the ramparts, the barricades and the breaches of Danzig, and the whole line of defence with them, but the siege was in the end decided by siege guns and by the sealing of the river mouth, not by pikes; within a few years even the last European army that kept the pike had taken to the bayonet, and from then on the pike survived only in ceremony, in drill books and in the memory of old soldiers.
